name: Blind
text: Can’t see. Attacks against you have advantage, and your attacks have disadvantage.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Dazed
text: Heroes lose 1 action; monsters lose their move OR 1 attack on their next turn.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Dying
text: At 0 HP. Max 1 action. Taking damage while Dying causes 2 Wounds; a crit causes 3 instead.

source.note: Shorter Glossary entry (PDF 29, printed 56): “When a hero is at 0 HP (see Hit Points & Dying on pg. 9 for more).”

name: Empowered X
text: Attack damage increased by X.

source.note: Text from the separate Glossary entry. The Conditions list (PDF 6, printed 11) combines them: “Empowered/Weakened X. Attack damage increased/reduced by X.”

name: Weakened X
text: Attack damage decreased by X.

source.note: Text from the separate Glossary entry. The Conditions list (PDF 6, printed 11) combines them: “Empowered/Weakened X. Attack damage increased/reduced by X.”

name: Frightened
text: Disadvantage on rolls when source of fear is near; Speed halved when moving closer to it.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Incapacitated
text: Can’t do anything. Attacks against you have advantage, and melee attacks that hit, crit.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Invisible
text: Cannot be seen. Your attacks have advantage, and attacks against you have disadvantage.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Poisoned
text: Disadvantage (typically, healing ends).

source.note: Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56) reads “Disadvantage on rolls (typically, healing ends).”

name: Prone
text: Movement costs twice as much, and disadvantage on attacks. Melee attacks against you have advantage; Ranged have disadvantage. Spend 3 spaces of your Speed to stand up.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Restrained
text: Can’t move. Attacks against you have advantage.

source.note: Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56): “Cannot move. Attacks against you have advantage.” Also under Grappling, Riding, & Restrained (PDF 6, printed 10): “Held by something rather than someone (sticky tar, chains, rope, roots): you can’t move, and attacks against you have advantage.” Breaking Free box (printed 10): escaping takes an action and a STR or DEX save, or other sensible means.

name: Silenced
text: Cannot cast spells or use other abilities that require speaking (e.g., Commander’s Orders).

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Slowed
text: Speed halved during your next turn.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Taunted
text: Disadvantage on attacks except against the most recent taunter.

source.note: Same text also in the Glossary (PDF 29, printed 56).

name: Bloodied
text: At half HP or less.

name: Charged
text: Some spells/abilities have additional effects when Charged (e.g., Overload, Electrickery). Become Charged whenever you take lightning damage. Lasts 1 min or until combat ends.

name: Charmed
text: Sees the charmer as an ally. Charmer has advantage on social interactions with you.

name: Deafened
text: Can’t hear.

name: Distracted
text: A target is Distracted if it is adjacent to or Taunted by an ally, or if it cannot see you.

source.note: Also named in the Other Minor/Rare Statuses box (PDF 6, printed 11).

name: Grappled
text: Held by another creature; attacks against either of you have advantage (see Grappling, Riding, & Restrained on pg. 10 for more).

source.note: Full Grappling rule under Grappling, Riding, & Restrained (PDF 6, printed 10): “Use an action to make a DC 10 Might or Finesse check on a creature your size or smaller to Grapple it: Attacks against either of you have advantage. If it’s smaller, it can’t move, but you can drag it along when you move; if you’re the same size, either of you can move at half Speed together.”

name: Hampered
text: Any creature with actions or movement reduced (e.g., Dazed, Grappled/Restrained, Prone, Slowed, in Difficult Terrain).

name: Paralyzed
text: Incapacitated. Can’t do anything. Attacks against you have advantage, and melee attacks that hit, crit.

source.note: Glossary entry “Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious.” covers three statuses; split into three entries with the same text.

name: Stunned
text: Incapacitated. Can’t do anything. Attacks against you have advantage, and melee attacks that hit, crit.

source.note: Glossary entry “Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious.” covers three statuses; split into three entries with the same text.

name: Unconscious
text: Incapacitated. Can’t do anything. Attacks against you have advantage, and melee attacks that hit, crit.

source.note: Glossary entry “Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious.” covers three statuses; split into three entries with the same text.

name: Petrified
text: Incapacitated with all the benefits and drawbacks of being a rock! Immune to most damage except from large explosions, picks, or similar tools.

name: Riding
text: You move with the creature you’re riding; it attacks you with disadvantage, and attacks that miss you strike it (see Grappling, Riding, & Restrained on pg. 10 for more).

source.note: Also under Grappling, Riding, & Restrained (PDF 6, printed 10): “Grab a bigger creature and you’re Riding it instead: you move with it, it attacks you with disadvantage, and attacks that miss you strike it.”

name: Smoldering
text: This condition does nothing on its own, though some spells and abilities have additional effects against Smoldering creatures, ending the condition (e.g., Ignite, Pyroclasm).

source.note: Also named in the Other Minor/Rare Statuses box (PDF 6, printed 11).

name: Wounded
text: Has any Wounds.
